name: FinchDB
tagline: Finch Computing's short-lived in-memory, JSON-style document and search analytics engine from 2015.
description: FinchDB was a proprietary in-memory analytics engine released around 2015 by Finch Computing, a text-analytics company now known as FinchAI. It stored JSON-style documents in memory across a distributed cluster and combined document storage with search-engine style querying, so the entities and relationships extracted by Finch's natural-language tools could be filtered and aggregated interactively. It was never sold or documented widely as a standalone database: the product page disappeared after 2016, DB-Engines lists it as discontinued, and FinchAI today markets entity extraction and risk-intelligence products rather than a database. Very little technical detail survives, so treat this entry as a historical marker.
statusNote: Product page gone since about 2016 and listed as discontinued by DB-Engines; Finch Computing (now FinchAI) no longer offers it.

pricing.notes: Was available only commercially; no longer offered.

strengths: Combined document storage with search-style filtering in memory for interactive analysis
Built to sit behind Finch's entity-extraction pipeline
weaknesses: Discontinued, with almost no surviving documentation
Never available as a general-purpose, independently supported product
useCases: Context for legacy Finch Computing analytics deployments
